title: Kunti
hook: in hiding at Ekachakra, Kunti hears her host's family weeping over whose turn it is to die, and offers one of her own sons instead

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kunti at the chariot, asking Krishna for troubles to come again, because in trouble she saw him. When something went wrong, did you look for what it showed you? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-six.

Through a thin wall, in a borrowed room, a mother hears another family crying. Years before the war, after the house of lac burned, Kunti and her sons are hiding in a town called Ekachakra, dressed as poor brahmins, living with a brahmin family who took them in. One evening the house fills with weeping. Kunti goes to find out why. Tomorrow, the family tells her, it is their turn. A demon named Baka lives near the town, and each household in turn must send him a cart of food and a person to be eaten with it. Now they're arguing over who should go. Today: what Kunti says next.
screen: `A BORROWED ROOM IN EKACHAKRA.` → `THE HOST FAMILY WEEPS.` → `IT'S THEIR TURN TOMORROW.`

segments.voice: The scene is in the Mahabharata's first book, and it starts with the family. The father says he will go. The mother says no, she will; he can find another wife, but the children need a father. The daughter says send me; I'm the one you'll lose to marriage anyway. And the small son picks up a blade of grass, waves it, and says he'll kill the demon with that. Then Kunti speaks, here in paraphrase. You have sheltered us. Let me repay you. I have five sons; one of them will take the food to Baka. The brahmin refuses. He can't let a guest die for him. Kunti insists, and tells him the son she has in mind is strong. When the brothers come home, Yudhishthira is upset. You're risking our brother on a stranger's trouble? Kunti's answer is calm. She has thought it through. She has seen Bhima's strength since he was a baby. And repaying the people who sheltered them is dharma; the town, too, will be better for it. So Bhima goes, eats the demon's food in front of him to make him angry, and kills him. What does the scene show about her? It's a portrait of a mother who doesn't panic. She weighs it, and decides. It's about debt. She's a guest, and to her a guest owes something to the house. And it shows a woman steering the family. Her eldest son questions her. The decision is hers.
screen: `EACH ONE OFFERS TO GO` · `LET ME REPAY YOU` · `A MOTHER WHO WEIGHS IT CALMLY` · `THE DECISION IS HERS`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember who sheltered you. Sit comfortably and let the breath slow. Bring to mind a time someone took you in: a room, a meal, a job, a hand when you needed it. Let their face come clearly. Notice whether anything feels unrepaid. You don't have to fix it now. Kunti took a moment to weigh things, and so can you. Just hold that person with each breath, and let one small way of thanking them occur to you. If you pray, you can give thanks for them. The bell holds the time.
Kunti. In hiding at Ekachakra, she offered one of her own sons to repay the family who sheltered them, and she didn't panic. Today's word.
Your line: Kunti. Today, do one small thing for someone who once took you in, the way Kunti repaid her host. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-six.

howItsDone: Hindus meet the Ekachakra story in retellings of the Mahabharata, in children's books and in storytelling, often told as Bhima's adventure, with Kunti's choice at its center.

fork.setup: you're Kunti, hiding in a stranger's house. your host's family must send one of their own to a demon tomorrow. what do you do?

offer one of your own sons to go.

fork.reveal: she offers one of her five sons, insists when the brahmin refuses, and calmly explains herself to Yudhishthira.

original.note: Sanskrit: born Pritha, raised by King Kuntibhoja, and called Kunti for him. Arjuna is called Partha, Pritha's son.

trapdoor: what you thought: Kunti is the quiet mother in the background.
what it means: at Ekachakra, she offers her son to repay a host, and explains her choice to her eldest.
what a scholar hears: the family's offers, the boy with the blade of grass, and a mother who weighs it and decides.

notes: Confirm the Ekachakra details: father, mother and daughter each offer to go; the small son brandishes a blade of grass; Kunti offers one of her five sons; the brahmin refuses to let a guest die; Yudhishthira objects and Kunti explains, citing Bhima's strength and the duty to repay the host; Bhima eats the food before Baka.
'She has seen Bhima's strength since he was a baby' alludes to the Adi Parva story of infant Bhima falling from Kunti's lap and shattering a rock; it is kept vague on purpose.
Mother's line 'he can find another wife' is a compressed paraphrase of her argument; check tone.
Original-game note: Pritha adopted by Kuntibhoja, and Arjuna as Partha, are in the Adi Parva; confirm wording.
